Description - AddFolder

Creates a folder named name under the parent newFolderId (0 = root) and returns its id.

**Errors (status Error + errorMessage):** EmptyName, InvalidCharacters, NameExistsAtDestination, FolderNotExists (unknown parent).

When the client sends it: folder tree "add folder" and the uploader's directory scan (box:folderPseudoId tracks the pending node).

Routing. The path item declares the server http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=, so this operation resolves to http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/AddFolder. WCF ignores the query string and dispatches only on the SOAPAction header (verified live). The real client posts to the bare http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc; both URLs reach the same operation. A path suffix (.svc/AddFolder) does not work (a:DestinationUnreachable, see soapRestStylePath).

Wire format. POST with Content-Type: text/xml;charset=utf-8 (exact client bytes, no space; the server answers text/xml; charset=utf-8) and SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/AddFolder (unquoted). Body: SOAP 1.1 envelope, UTF-8, no indentation, parameters in the documented order (WCF silently drops out-of-order parameters). The client gzips the body (Content-Encoding: gzip).

Path notes

SOAP operation AddFolder. The path-level server makes the URL routable: WCF dispatches on SOAPAction and ignores the ?op=/AddFolder query.

WCF dispatch key. The client sends it unquoted (SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/AddFolder); a quoted value works too. Missing or unknown actions give a:ActionNotSupported.

http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/AddFolder
Content-Encodingheaderoptionalstring one of "gzip"

Present when the body is gzip-compressed ([network] soap-use-gzip=true in the default config; zlib level -1, windowBits 31). Accepted by the service (Auth/success vs Auth/success-uncompressed-request).

Schema

Schema AddFolderRequestEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required AddFolderRequestEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 request envelope for AddFolder: <s:Envelope><s:Body><AddFolder xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/">…. No SOAP header is ever sent; xmlns:i is declared on the operation element only when a nil value is present.

    • @s:encodingStyle string optional = "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/encoding/" namespace http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

      SOAP 1.1 encodingStyle attribute. The real client always writes it; the service accepts the envelope with or without it.

    • <s:Body> object required

      Exactly one operation element; no other content (this also makes the per-operation envelopes mutually exclusive).

      • <AddFolder> object required AddFolderRequest xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

        Operation element AddFolder in http://chomikuj.pl/ (trailing slash is mandatory: with http://chomikuj.pl the parameters are not matched, see Service/wrong-operation-namespace).

        • <token> string required Token

          Session token. Always the first child.

        • <newFolderId> integer (int32) required

          Parent folder id (0 = account root), despite the name (verified live).

        • <name> string required

          Name of the new folder. Empty gives EmptyName; / : * ? and similar give InvalidCharacters; a duplicate gives NameExistsAtDestination.

Responses - 200, 500

200

SOAP response envelope. HTTP 200 is used for every service-level outcome, including errors: check AddFolderResult/status. Compressed (Content-Encoding: gzip) when the request accepts gzip.

Schema text/xml

Schema AddFolderResponseEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required AddFolderResponseEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 response envelope for AddFolder: <s:Envelope><s:Body><AddFolderResponse xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/"><AddFolderResult …>.

    • <s:Body> object required

      Exactly one response element; no other content.

      • <AddFolderResponse> object required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/
        • <AddFolderResult> object required AddFolderResult

          Result element; declares xmlns:i (XML Schema instance, for i:nil) and xmlns:a.

          • <status> string required Status xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Outcome of the call. Serialised as <status xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl"> (default-namespace redeclaration, no prefix) in this result type.

            7 values
            • "Ok" Success. The only value the client treats as success.
            • "BadToken" Unknown, logged-out or otherwise invalid token. The client re-authenticates (Auth) once per message (message-relog-count=1) and resends the message with the new token; session-bound messages are dropped.
            • "Forbidden" Auth: user name does not exist. The client shows the credentials dialog.
            • "PermissionError" Auth: wrong password for an existing user. The client shows the credentials dialog.
            • "Error" Generic failure. Usually carries a reason in errorMessage (e.g. EmptyName, NameExistsAtDestination); FolderFiles with an unknown disposition returns Error with errorMessage nil (FolderFiles/invalid-disposition).
            • "NotEmptyOrNotExistsFolder" RemoveFolder with force=false on a folder that contains files, or on an unknown/removed folder id.
            • "WrongDisposition" FolderFiles: the disposition is a known value but not allowed for this call (download).
          • <errorMessage> string required nullable (i:nil) ErrorMessage xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Error detail for status=Error; nil otherwise. Same namespace treatment as status.

          • <a:folderId> integer (int32) required xmlns http://schemas.datacontract.org/2004/07/TeamSolutions.Chomik.DAO.ChomikBox

            Id of the created folder; 0 on error.

500 SoapFault

WCF SOAP fault (HTTP 500, Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8, not compressed). Possible for every SOAP operation: an empty or malformed body gives a:InternalServiceFault, an undeserialisable value a:DeserializationFailed, an unknown or missing SOAPAction a:ActionNotSupported. Operations with an operation-specific captured fault document it inline instead.

Schema text/xml

Schema SoapFaultEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required SoapFaultEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 fault envelope (HTTP 500, Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8, never gzip-compressed).

    • <s:Body> object required
      • <s:Fault> object required SoapFault

        The fault.

        • <faultcode> string required no namespace

          Qualified fault code with its own namespace declaration on the element: a:InternalServiceFault and a:DeserializationFailed (a = http://schemas.microsoft.com/net/2005/12/windowscommunicationfoundation/dispatcher), a:ActionNotSupported and a:DestinationUnreachable (a = http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2005/05/addressing/none).

        • <faultstring> object required no namespace

          Human-readable message. DeserializationFailed names the parameter and CLR type, which is how the contract was established.

          • @xml:lang string required namespace http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace

            Language of the message (en-US).

          • text content string required

            Message text.

Client vs live - discrepancies

Where the client's expected behaviour and the live service disagree, the spec follows the live behaviour (x-discrepancies):

  • Result has only folderId; the client also expects folderName, prevModifyTime, modifyTime.
  • Result members are in the DAO datacontract namespace.
